references.text: Isaiah describes how human hands grow weak and every human heart melts with fear on the Lord's day: 'Therefore all hands will fall limp, and every human heart will melt. They are terrified; pangs and sorrows seize them' (Isaiah 13:7-8). This corresponds to Luke's description of people perishing from fear.

Isaiah prophesies about the dissolution of the host of heaven: 'All the host of heaven shall rot away, and the skies roll up like a scroll' (Isaiah 34:4). This is directly linked to the statement that 'the powers of the heavens will be shaken.'
Joel describes cosmic signs on the Lord's day: 'The sun and the moon are darkened, and the stars cease to shine' (Joel 2:10). The shaking of the powers of the heavens in Luke parallels this.

Haggai conveys the word of the Lord: 'Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land. I will shake all nations' (Haggai 2:6-7). The shaking of the powers of the heavens in Luke is a fulfillment of this prophecy.
Earlier in the same discourse, Jesus speaks of great signs from heaven (Luke 21:11), which prepares for the cosmic shaking described in verse 26.
The preceding verse (Luke 21:25) describes signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and the distress of nations on earth, forming the immediate context for the fear described in verse 26.
Matthew's parallel passage states that 'the powers of the heavens will be shaken' after the sun is darkened and the moon gives no light (Matthew 24:29). This is the synoptic parallel to Luke 21:26b.
Mark's parallel says that 'the powers of the heavens will be shaken' (Mark 13:25), which directly corresponds to Luke's wording.

The Epistle to the Hebrews quotes Haggai and says: 'Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heaven' (Hebrews 12:26-27). This confirms the idea of the powers of the heavens being shaken.

Revelation describes cosmic chaos and people hiding in fear, crying out to the mountains: 'Fall on us and hide us' (Revelation 6:13-17). The human reaction of deep fear toward the cosmic signs corresponds directly to Luke 21:26.
